pr.title: Introduce debuginfo to statements in MIR
pr.description:
The PR introduces support for debug information within dead statements. Currently, only the reference statement is supported, which is sufficient to fix rust-lang/rust#128081.

I don't modify Stable MIR, as I don't think we need debug information when using it.

This PR represents the debug information for the dead reference statement via `#dbg_value`. For example, `let _foo_b = &foo.b` becomes `#dbg_value(ptr %foo, !22, !DIExpression(DW_OP_plus_uconst, 4, DW_OP_stack_value), !26)`. You can see this here: https://rust.godbolt.org/z/d43js6adv.

The general principle for handling debug information is to never provide less debug information than the optimized LLVM IR.

The current rules for dropping debug information in this PR are:

- If the LLVM IR cannot represent a reference address, it's replaced with poison or simply dropped. For example, see: https://rust.godbolt.org/z/shGqPec8W. I'm using poison in all such cases now.
- All debuginfos is dropped when merging multiple successor BBs. An example is available here: https://rust.godbolt.org/z/TE1q3Wq6M.

I doesn't drop debuginfos in `MatchBranchSimplification`, because LLVM also pick one branch for it.

processing.reason: The historical PR changes MIR/debuginfo bookkeeping only: SimplifyCfg relocates or drops `StmtDebugInfo`, Inline changes `always_live_locals` and drops callee debuginfos, and StripDebugInfo filters statement-level debuginfo. The regression tests are MIR-dump/FileCheck tests (`//@ test-mir-pass`, `EMIT_MIR`, `// DBG:` checks), not execution tests. None of the changed operations affects program values, memory contents, control flow reaching real statements, or anything observable by Miri. Encoding the debuginfo relocation as ordinary runtime data would be an unrelated invented transformation, not the historical compiler rewrite, and would not satisfy the requirement that both functions are the same original/incorrect source pair with identical inputs. Therefore no source-grounded executable counterexample can be validated for this PR's changes.

analysis.summary: Statement-level debuginfo must be relocated or dropped explicitly when CFG blocks are merged, inlined, retained, or stripped. SimplifyCfg may propagate debuginfos through a goto chain only when every successor has a single predecessor; when multiple predecessor blocks merge, branch-local debuginfos must be dropped. Inline must seed always-live locals from actual statement uses and drop callee debuginfos when debuginfo is not being emitted, while StripDebugInfo must filter both per-statement and after-last-statement debuginfos.
analysis.originalLogic: In `CfgSimplifier::merge_blocks`, the old merge moved only `statements` and the terminator: `let mut statements = std::mem::take(&mut self.basic_blocks[bb].statements);` then appended each `from` block's statements. There was no `after_last_stmt_debuginfos` slot, so once statement-level debuginfo was introduced, merging or collapsing blocks had no place to carry debuginfos that occurred after the last statement. `collapse_goto_chain` retargeted goto targets without tracking whether each successor had multiple predecessors. Inline constructed the inliner with `always_live_locals: DenseBitSet::new_filled(callee_body.local_decls.len())`, marking every callee local live, and only appended callee `var_debug_info` when debuginfo was being emitted. `StripDebugInfo` removed only `var_debug_info` entries and did not filter statement-level `StmtDebugInfo`.
analysis.incorrectTransformation: A naive CFG merge that moves statements but leaves or propagates `after_last_stmt_debuginfos` unchanged can associate a debug value with a path that was not taken, or lose the debug value when a block disappears. The correct behavior differs by CFG shape: for a trivial goto chain where each successor has exactly one predecessor, debuginfos can be prepended to the target's first statement or its after-last slot; for a merge point reached from multiple predecessor BBs, all such debuginfos must be dropped because it is ambiguous which path executed. The source explicitly keeps `MatchBranchSimplification` from dropping debuginfos because LLVM also picks one branch. Inline should not mark every callee local always-live, and should not propagate callee statement debuginfos when debuginfo is not emitted; `StripDebugInfo` must remove `StmtDebugInfo::AssignRef`/`InvalidAssign` entries whose local is stripped from both `stmt.debuginfos` and `after_last_stmt_debuginfos`. Test pairs should be identical except for CFG shape: a single-predecessor goto chain should preserve the debuginfo, while adding a second predecessor to the merge target should make it disappear.
analysis.inputDomain: MIR after inlining/cleanup with `BasicBlockData::after_last_stmt_debuginfos`; CFGs containing goto chains, `switchInt` with identical or distinct successors, and blocks whose last real statement was eliminated so the debuginfo lives after the last statement. Also inlined callee bodies with locals that are unused except in debuginfo, and modes where debuginfo is not emitted or `-Zstrip-debuginfo` filters variables. Use custom MIR so the CFG and debuginfo placement are exact.
analysis.trigger: SimplifyCfg merges or collapses basic blocks that carry `after_last_stmt_debuginfos` or per-statement debuginfos; Inline adds a callee body with unused locals and debuginfo; StripDebugInfo removes a local that appears in statement-level debuginfo.
preconditions: `BasicBlockData` has an `after_last_stmt_debuginfos` slot for debuginfos that occur after the last statement and before the terminator.
When merging blocks, the parent's pending debuginfos are prepended to the first statement of the first merged block, or carried in the after-last slot if no statement exists.
A goto chain is treated as trivial only when every successor has exactly one predecessor (`trivial_goto_chain &= self.pred_count[target] == 1;`).
At a merge with multiple predecessor BBs, debuginfos from the merged/eliminated paths are dropped.
Inline's `always_live_locals` is derived from `UsedInStmtLocals::new(&callee_body).locals`, not all locals, and callee debuginfos are dropped when the caller should not emit debuginfo.
StripDebugInfo filters statement-level debuginfos by `debuginfo_locals`, including `InvalidAssign`, in both statement and after-last slots.
pitfalls: Do not propagate debuginfo through a non-trivial goto chain or a block with multiple predecessors; doing so can claim a value was computed on a path that did not execute.
Do not drop debuginfos in `MatchBranchSimplification`; the PR explicitly preserves them because LLVM picks one branch.
When merging, preserve ordering by prepending pending debuginfos before the first statement of each merged block, and carry the last merged block's after-last debuginfos to the parent.
If a block has no statements, debuginfos belong in `after_last_stmt_debuginfos`, not on a nonexistent statement.
Inline must not keep all callee locals live merely because they exist; use actual statement uses so dead locals and storage can be removed.
If debuginfo is not emitted, drop callee statement debuginfos before appending the callee blocks; otherwise stale variables from the inlined body survive.
StripDebugInfo must handle both `StmtDebugInfo::AssignRef` and `StmtDebugInfo::InvalidAssign`, and must filter `after_last_stmt_debuginfos` as well as `stmt.debuginfos`.
`retain_statements` must move debuginfos from removed statements to the next retained statement or to the after-last slot; raw `Vec::retain` loses them.
analysis.testStrategy: Use `tests/mir-opt/debuginfo/simplifycfg.rs` with `//@ test-mir-pass: SimplifyCfg-final` and `//@ compile-flags: -Zmir-enable-passes=+DeadStoreElimination-initial`, writing `#[custom_mir(dialect = \"runtime\", phase = \"post-cleanup\")]` functions. Cover: (1) `drop_debuginfo`: `switchInt` sends one edge through a block that computes `foo_a` then merges into a block reached from both paths; expect `foo_a` DBG to be absent from the merged block and `foo_b` to remain. (2) `preserve_debuginfo_1`/`preserve_debuginfo_2`: a pure goto chain where each block has one predecessor; expect all DBG entries to be prepended in order into the final `bb0`. (3) `preserve_debuginfo_3`: `switchInt` with distinct successors; expect `foo_a` only in the true branch and `foo_b` only in the false branch, with no cross-branch contamination. (4) `preserve_debuginfo_identical_succs`: both switch edges target the same block; expect all DBG entries preserved in one block. For Inline, use `tests/mir-opt/inline/inline_shims.drop.*` and `inline_coroutine_body.*` to check that redundant `StorageLive`/`StorageDead` locals disappear while remaining behavior is unchanged. For unrepresentable references, use `tests/mir-opt/pre-codegen/dead_on_invalid_place.rs` and expect `// DBG: _2 = &?;`. Use FileCheck `CHECK-NEXT` to pin debuginfo ordering and verify absence where a merge must drop it; do not claim execution without running the tests.
evidence: All debuginfos is dropped when merging multiple successor BBs. An example is available here: https://rust.godbolt.org/z/TE1q3Wq6M.
I doesn't drop debuginfos in `MatchBranchSimplification`, because LLVM also pick one branch for it.
